Senses.Explanation: A measured metaphor unit naming the inherited endowment as one whole field, handed over long ago and left open for all to till. Xuefeng Yicun, recorded in his disciple's extensive log, declares the matter like one whole stretch of field left for everyone to till, with none who fail to owe it strength; Xuansha Shibei, preserved in Dahui's old-case verses, deeds away the field's four borders to all while keeping only the center tree for the old monk; and Huitang Zuxin laments heirs who let the handed-down field run to brambles while chasing daily grain, telling them to claim the original deed with its borders plain. Yuanwu Keqin runs his hall address through false takes at the staff's head and the shout below before landing on the field handed over long ago and plain deceit; Dahui Zonggao holds that one who knows where this whole field lands cannot be moved a hair by birth and death; Buhui Fatong answers the elders' chain by refusing any re-deed, since the field needs no handing over and the four directions are nowhere else; Juelang Daosheng judges the Xuefeng and Xuansha pair as leaving the field mutually abandoned and answers the asking with a staff; and Zhe'an Jingfan tells the assembly everyone has this field, which no season has ever dared damage, so why redraw its bounds.
